purpose: Add the Moon as an independent factual Tempus trajectory on the existing seventy-two-sector dodecahedral/icosahedral carrier while proving that the solar-driven ARCnet transport, Vitae state, and authority contracts remain invariant under lunar motion.

external_references.finding: Horizons identifies the Moon center as target 301, Earth center as 399, and observer quantity 31 as observer-centered apparent ecliptic-of-date longitude/latitude.

external_references.source: JPL Lunar Constants and Models Document D-32296
external_references.finding: JPL states that strict new Moon occurs when the apparent ecliptic longitudes of Moon and Sun, viewed from Earth's center, are equal.

external_references.source: NASA Scientific Visualization Studio, Moon Phase and Libration 2026
external_references.finding: NASA renders the 2026 Moon geocentrically at hourly intervals and explains that lunar phases arise from the changing Sun-Moon-Earth angle; the lunar orbit is inclined about five degrees to the ecliptic.

external_references.source: NASA Scientific Visualization Studio, August 27-28 2026 Deep Partial Lunar Eclipse
external_references.finding: NASA gives greatest eclipse as 2026-08-28T04:13Z and reports 96.3 percent of the lunar disk inside Earth's umbra, providing a current alignment test for longitude-plus-latitude modeling.

independent_trajectories.shared_shell_rule: Sharing the same neutral longitude coordinate does not make Sun and Moon the same clock, role, or authority source.

prototype_snapshot.production_note: This snapshot validates the resolver and independent-motion model but is not represented as a JPL Horizons response. Production should ingest explicitly sourced Horizons/SPICE-equivalent data.

eclipse_falsification_case.finding: The Moon is almost exactly opposite the Sun in longitude at greatest eclipse, while lunar latitude remains nonzero. Eclipse state therefore cannot be reduced to a one-dimensional 180-degree rule; finite body/shadow geometry and latitude matter.
eclipse_falsification_case.architecture_effect: Tempus may display eclipse context only from a separately sourced astronomical event/geometry computation; ordinary longitude opposition never becomes an eclipse claim by itself.
